title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: keep sensitive windows out of Windows Recall snapshots on Copilot+ PCs (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing, Recall restrictions and device controls are supported by Microsoft's documentation. The Purview editing path is supported across the cited policy-editing and Recall pages, and the corrected distinction between auditing and blocking is accurate.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Governance controls
claims.claim: The new DLP control requires administrator configuration of a Purview rule and the Windows provider policy.
claims.quote: Set the following Group Policy settings on the Copilot+ PC to enable DLP protections for Recall using either Microsoft Intune or Local Group Policy Editor. The setting to enable DLP protections for Recall is available when you create or edit a DLP policy

claims.claim: The printed Purview policy-editing path reaches Restrict content in Windows Recall.
claims.quote: under Actions > Audit or restrict activities on devices > Restrictions in Windows Recall in Copilot+ PCs > Restrict content in Windows Recall

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an automation operation that sets the Purview Recall rule restriction.
claims.quote: Searched: Recall DLP Set-DlpComplianceRule EndpointDlpRestrictions Windows Recall PowerShell restrict content. Opened Set-DlpComplianceRule and dlp-recall-get-started; read Recall DLP Provider API search excerpts. No Purview rule-setting operation or Recall setting value was documented.

claims.claim: The Recall restriction offers Audit only and Block in Enterprise applications & devices policies.
claims.quote: The setting to enable DLP protections for Recall is available when you create or edit a DLP policy in Enterprise Applications & devices policies. You can select Audit only or Block.

claims.claim: Audit only does not notify the user when a sensitive-content snapshot is taken.
claims.quote: If you select Audit only, then the user doesn't see any notification when a snapshot is taken that contains sensitive information.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Audit only logs sensitive-content snapshot events in DLP reports.
claims.quote: If you select Audit only, then the user doesn't see any notification when a snapshot is taken that contains sensitive information. However, the event is logged in the DLP reports.

claims.claim: Audit only allows the sensitive-content capture rather than blocking the window.
claims.quote: Audit only: The user activity is allowed to occur, so no business processes are impacted. You get audit data

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Block excludes sensitive content from the Recall snapshot.
claims.quote: If you select Block, then when a snapshot is taken that contains sensitive information, then the sensitive content isn't included in the snapshot.

claims.claim: DLP enforcement removes the identified windows while retaining the rest of the snapshot.
claims.quote: DLP enforcement is applied at the window level—Recall removes only the specific window(s) identified by the DLP provider as containing sensitive data blocked by policy, while retaining the rest of the snapshot.

claims.quote: Files stored in the cloud that with sensitivity labels or SITS that get opened in Office apps (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) on the device

claims.claim: Recall is disabled and removed by default on managed devices.
claims.quote: By default, Recall is disabled and removed on managed devices.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope: Users; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Saving snapshots requires each user's opt-in consent after administrators make Recall available.
claims.quote: Recall is an opt-in experience that requires end user consent to save snapshots. IT admins can only set policies that give users the option to enable saving snapshots

claims.claim: IT administrators cannot start saving snapshots for end users.
claims.quote: IT admins, on their own, can't start saving snapshots for end users.

claims.claim: Recall's Sensitive information filtering is enabled by default.
claims.quote: When using Recall, the Sensitive information filtering setting is enabled by default to help ensure your data's confidentiality.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Opted-in Recall snapshots can contain labelled or SIT-matching content without a blocking DLP restriction.
claims.quote: If you select Audit only, then the user doesn't see any notification when a snapshot is taken that contains sensitive information.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described how Recall's Sensitive information filtering combines with a Purview rule.
claims.quote: Searched: Recall Sensitive information filtering Purview DLP Block interaction licensing meter. Opened manage-recall, dlp-recall-get-started and recall-sensitive-information-filtering; read DLP Provider API search excerpts. No interaction or precedence between the two filters was stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The Recall DLP Learn page lists no other app or content categories beyond the stated coverage.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview Recall DLP protections Recall Set Data Loss Prevention Provider. Opened dlp-recall-get-started in full: its supported-content list contains Teams channels, Teams meeting chats, Copilot app web files, Outlook emails, local files and cloud files opened in Office.

claims.claim: The printed Computer Configuration Group Policy path reaches Set Data Loss Prevention Provider.
claims.quote: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows AI > Set Data Loss Prevention Provider

claims.claim: The device WindowsAI/SetDataLossPreventionProvider CSP configures the DLP provider Recall uses.
claims.quote:
./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/WindowsAI/SetDataLossPreventionProvider
This policy allows an admin to specify a DLP provider, which Recall will use if the provider is properly installed.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: The provider policy applies to Enterprise and Education client SKUs only, not Pro.
claims.quote:
✅ Device  ❌ User | ❌ Pro  ✅ Enterprise  ✅ Education  ✅ IoT Enterprise / IoT Enterprise LTSC
This setting applies to Enterprise and Education client SKUs only.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Removing or clearing the provider policy stops Recall invoking a DLP provider.
claims.quote: Removing or clearing this policy stops Recall from invoking a DLP provider; previously stored snapshots remain unaffected.

claims.claim: Removing or clearing the provider policy does not affect previously stored snapshots.
claims.quote: Removing or clearing this policy stops Recall from invoking a DLP provider; previously stored snapshots remain unaffected.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set Data Loss Prevention Provider is required to enable DLP integration with Recall.
claims.quote: To enable DLP integration, set the Set Data Loss Prevention Provider policy on managed devices.

claims.claim: Purview is currently the only supported DLP provider for Recall.
claims.quote: Purview is currently the only supported DLP provider for Recall.

claims.claim: Manage Recall supplies a Purview provider value for Set Data Loss Prevention Provider.
claims.quote:
key:HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\software\microsoft\windows defender; value:InstallLocation; binary:endpointdlp.dll; minversion:4.18.25080.5
This enables Recall to use Microsoft Purview as the DLP provider.

claims.claim: The printed Computer Configuration Group Policy path reaches Turn off saving snapshots for Recall.
claims.quote: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows AI > Turn off saving snapshots for Recall

claims.claim: The device WindowsAI/DisableAIDataAnalysis CSP controls whether users may save Recall snapshots.
claims.quote:
./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/WindowsAI/DisableAIDataAnalysis
The Turn off saving snapshots for Recall policy allows you to give the users the choice to save snapshots of their screen for use with Recall.

claims.claim: The Recall DLP page instructs disabling Turn off saving snapshots so users can opt in.
claims.quote: WindowsAI > Turn off saving snapshots for use with Recall | Disable | Yes | This policy makes the Recall feature available to users to opt in. This doesn't automatically start Recall for users.

claims.claim: Enabling Turn off saving snapshots deletes snapshots previously saved on the device.
claims.quote: If snapshots were previously saved on a device, they'll be deleted when this policy is enabled.

claims.claim: The printed Computer Configuration Group Policy path reaches Allow Recall to be enabled.
claims.quote: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows AI > Allow Recall to be enabled

claims.claim: The device WindowsAI/AllowRecallEnablement CSP controls Recall availability on managed devices.
claims.quote:
./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/WindowsAI/AllowRecallEnablement
The Allow Recall to be enabled policy setting allows you to determine whether the Recall optional component is available for end users to enable on their device.

claims.claim: Disabling Allow Recall to be enabled deletes previously saved snapshots.
claims.quote: If snapshots were previously saved on the device, they'll be deleted when this policy is disabled.
